html:
SMTO-LLM-0039 — Model discovery failed

GUID: 7adc7f9c-d24b-4f50-8ad6-7308b54457ab
Slug: model-discovery-failed
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: llm

What happened

  • SMTO asked the model server which models it offers but didn't get a usable answer. No question was sent to the model, so nothing was run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the computer or service running the model is switched on, has finished starting, and can be reached from the computer running SMTO. SMTO stops waiting for the model list after a few seconds if the server doesn't answer.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, expand the affected model (Main, Helper or Vision), and confirm the Endpoint address and API key are correct. A wrong address or a rejected key stops the server from sending its model list.
  3. Select Check saved model, or turn off Auto-select model and select Discover models, to ask the server again. Both ask the server for its model list and show whether it now answers.

What success looks like

  • Discover models lists your model, or Check saved model reports passing checks.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who runs the model server or manages SMTO. Don't turn off connection or security checks to make the error go away.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The model endpoint's GET /models request failed, timed out, returned more than 4 MiB, or returned an empty or unparseable list, so SMTO could not verify the served models.

What this means

  • The discovery loader failed to retrieve or interpret the endpoint's model inventory; an inventory failure is not evidence that an inference request was dispatched. This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • The discovery loader failed to retrieve or interpret the endpoint's model inventory; an inventory failure is not evidence that an inference request was dispatched.

How to diagnose it

  • Check model-list connectivity, HTTP status and response shape at the configured endpoint; distinguish an unreachable list from a successfully returned empty list.

How to fix it

  • Request the configured base URL plus /models with the saved API key and confirm it returns a non-empty JSON model list within 5 seconds (NativeToolCallLLMClient._served_models in src/agent_runtime/llm/native_tool_client.py). Fix connectivity, authentication or the provider's model-list support, then use Discover models or Check saved model; this failure does not mean an inference request was sent.
  • Check endpoint connectivity, authentication and the provider’s model-list support, then refresh models. This discovery failure does not mean an inference request was sent.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Refreshing discovery returns a bounded list containing the intended model identity.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
